headline: Trump answers 'No' when asked if he is considering striking Iran after the midterm elections
dek: Asked by reporters after his closing midterm speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool whether he was considering striking Iran after the elections, Trump replied 'No.' Reuters frames it as raising doubts about following through on his threatened resumption of strikes; Trump added he believes…
sources: US President Donald Trump, on-camera exchange with reporters after Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool speech
fault_line: Deal or hammer, decided by one word: does Trump's 'No' mean the post-midterm strike threat is off -- or is it election-eve talk that reverses the morning after the votes are counted?

sections.what_happened: Asked by reporters after his closing midterm speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool whether he was considering striking Iran after the elections, Trump replied 'No.' Reuters frames it as raising doubts about following through on his threatened resumption of strikes; Trump added he believes Iran wants a deal and that a deal 'could happen,' while stressing the bottom line that Iran must never have a nuclear weapon. In a separate Axios phone interview the same day he said 'One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush.' This is a NEW on-record statement in-window: it softens the post-midterm 'hammer' threat (Nov 1 Dubuque rally, already recorded) on the eve of the Nov 3 vote. It is NOT a permanent pledge: Ynet/Reuters both note he did not rule out further action if diplomacy fails, and Vance the same evening said no deadline has been set.
sections.what_verified: Two declared-tier families for the quote itself (Reuters T1 wire; Ynetnews T3), plus the president's own on-camera words as primary source. JPost's version is a Reuters carry (same family, not independent). NY Post and TRT World carry the same exchange but hold no declared tier in the registry and are NOT counted.
sections.what_disputed: Axios, citing one Israeli and one US source, reported Netanyahu pressed Trump on their Saturday phone call to resume strikes immediately after the midterms, while Trump preferred letting diplomacy continue for now -- the 'No' sits against that pressure, not against a settled policy. Reuters also reported Iranian sources believing a new US attack was still more likely than a deal. Analyst Negar Mortazavi's AJ assessment (21:30 GMT, prior window) warned the post-midterm strike risk 'remains very real.' Trump's own 'one way or the other, we will do something' (Axios) keeps the military option live.
sections.why_matters: The word that moved the war: asked point-blank if he will strike Iran after the midterms, Trump answers 'No' -- hours after his own deputy said there is no deadline and days after he promised 'the hammer.' The catch, in his own next breath: 'one way or the other, we will do something.'
